name: Next.js
text: Next.js is the approved web front-end framework for customer-facing web apps, including checkout and account pages.

name: FastAPI
text: FastAPI (Python) is the approved framework for backend REST services and internal APIs.

name: PostgreSQL
text: PostgreSQL is the approved relational database for transactional data such as orders, wallets and ledgers.

name: Redis
text: Redis is the approved in-memory store for caching, sessions, idempotency keys, rate limiting and short-lived distributed locks.

name: Kafka
text: Kafka is the approved event streaming platform for asynchronous integration and domain events between services.
PCI-DSS: card data must be tokenised by the payment service provider; services handle only tokens, never raw card numbers.
PCI-DSS: never store the full card number (PAN) or the CVV/security code in any database, log or cache.
PCI-DSS: all access to payment functions and payment data must be recorded in a tamper-evident audit log.
PCI-DSS: payment-related data must be encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest.
GDPR: obtain explicit, recorded consent before storing personal data or payment methods for future use; consent must be withdrawable.
GDPR: data minimisation — collect and keep only the personal data needed for the stated purpose.
GDPR: right to erasure — customers can request deletion of their personal data and saved payment methods.
GDPR: define a retention period for each category of personal data and delete or anonymise it when the period ends.
Story points must use the Fibonacci scale [1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13]; split any story larger than 13.

Idempotency keys in Redis: every payment or checkout request carries a client-generated idempotency key; the service stores the key and result in Redis so retries and double clicks never create duplicate payments or orders.

Transactional outbox to Kafka: write the domain change and an outbox event in the same PostgreSQL transaction, then relay outbox rows to Kafka so events are never lost or published without the matching data change.

Distributed lock for wallet balance: take a short-lived Redis lock per wallet (plus a row-level lock in PostgreSQL) before debiting, so concurrent payments cannot double-spend or overdraw the wallet balance.

PSP tokenisation flow: the browser sends card details directly to the payment service provider's hosted fields, receives a token, and only the token is sent to our backend and stored for one-click payments.
